paper_metadata.title: Derivative Pricing using Quantum Signal Processing

summary: The paper proposes a QSP-based method for derivative pricing that replaces quantum arithmetic in payoff evaluation. For the autocallable benchmark, it reports 4.7k logical qubits, T-depth 4.5×10^7, and T-count 2.4×10^9 for the Usqrt-based QSP approach, improving over an arithmetic baseline by about 4.1× in qubits, 4.7× in T-depth, and 16× in T-count. The European call example is illustrative and includes polynomial approximations of degrees 6, 8, and 16, but no full resource benchmark or hardware result.

experiments.description: QSP-based pricing of a European call option by replacing quantum arithmetic in the payoff operator with amplitude transformation; uses a discretized log-return distribution and QSP to encode the payoff amplitude.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Signal Processing (QSP) for derivative payoff encoding; European call option pricing with QSP-based payoff operator

hyperparameters.binary_point_digits: p digits to the left of the binary point

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Log-returns are loaded in a superposition; a comparator and QSP are used to encode the payoff amplitude directly without computing explicit payoff values in a separate register.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate the expected payoff of a European call option, E[max(0, S_T-K)] normalized by fmax, via amplitude estimation on the payoff ancilla.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Comparator-based thresholding to separate in-the-money paths; QSP polynomial approximates the payoff-related amplitude function on [0,1].

problem_instance.description: European call option on a single underlying asset.

dataset_specification.description: Discretized normal distribution over log-returns; example plot uses S0=K=100, p=3, s=0.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Load discretized normal distribution of log-returns; compute threshold s=ln(S0/K); compare ri to s; add |s| shift and apply QSP to the shifted register.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Illustrative circuit construction and polynomial approximation; no empirical sampling study reported.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Discretize log-return distribution; compute threshold s=ln(S0/K).
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Amplitude estimation on the payoff ancilla to recover normalized option price.

speedup_claims.caveats: The paper discusses the European call option as an illustrative construction and does not provide a direct numerical comparison or benchmark for this example.

complexity_analysis.constant_factor_quantum: ~16x fewer T-gates and ~4x fewer logical qubits versus prior arithmetic-based approach for the broader autocallable benchmark; no asymptotic order stated for this specific option.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: No end-to-end resource estimate is reported for the European call example; the section is methodological and illustrative only.
limiting_factors: No classical-vs-quantum benchmark for this specific option

experiments.description: QSP-based pricing of a single-asset autocallable derivative, replacing quantum register exponentiation in the payoff computation with QSP on the final timestep.

algorithm.variant: QSP-based autocallable pricing; compares Usin-based QSP and Usqrt-based QSP
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Polynomial approximation error max |f(x)-P(x)| <= 1e-3 for payoff amplitude

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Log-returns for all assets and timesteps are prepared via reparameterization; payoff conditions are computed with ancilla qubits; final payoff clause is encoded by QSP directly on the shifted final return register.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Price an autocallable contract by estimating the expected payoff, including binary autocall triggers and a barrier-contingent final payoff.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Binary payoff trigger qubits s_i and barrier qubit b are computed with comparator/CNOT/Toffoli logic; final payoff clause is conditioned on b and uses QSP to encode sqrt(1-(K_T-e^{r_T})) or equivalent amplitude.

problem_instance.description: Autocallable derivative on a single underlying asset, benchmarked for a = 3 assets and T = 20 timesteps in the resource estimate section; includes binary payoffs and a barrier condition.

dataset_specification.description: Geometric Brownian motion / multivariate lognormal log-return model with parameters (mu, Sigma) from historical market values; no specific market dataset named.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Prepare independent standard normal registers N(0,1), transform to multivariate normal N(mu,Sigma), compute payoff trigger bits s_i and barrier bits b_t from log-returns, shift final return by s=R to make amplitudes positive.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Analytical resource estimation and explicit circuit construction; polynomial approximation error checked for KT=1 and target epsilon_p=1e-3; resources compared against prior arithmetic-based implementation.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Load multivariate normal distribution N(mu,Sigma); compute payoff trigger conditions and barrier conditions using comparator logic; choose s=R to shift final return into [0,1].
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Iterative Quantum Amplitude Estimation used to estimate the target amplitude to within epsilon=1e-3 at confidence 0.68.

speedup_claims.conditions: autocallable benchmark with a = 3 assets, T = 20 timesteps, epsilon = 2e-3, epsilon_p = 1e-3; comparing Usqrt-QSP to arithmetic baseline
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports 36k vs 7.8k T-depth in Table 1, corresponding to about 4.7x improvement.

speedup_claims.conditions: autocallable benchmark with a = 3 assets, T = 20 timesteps, epsilon = 2e-3, epsilon_p = 1e-3; comparing Usqrt-QSP to arithmetic baseline
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports 6.6M vs 414k T-count, corresponding to about 16x improvement.

speedup_claims.conditions: autocallable benchmark with a = 3 assets, T = 20 timesteps, epsilon = 2e-3, epsilon_p = 1e-3; comparing Usqrt-QSP to arithmetic baseline
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports 19.2k vs 4.7k logical qubits, corresponding to about 4.1x reduction.

speedup_claims.factor: logical clock rate reduced from 207 MHz to 45 MHz
speedup_claims.conditions: end-to-end quantum advantage estimate for pricing the autocallable contract; classical runtime assumed to be 1 second
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a resource-rate estimate rather than a direct hardware benchmark.

speedup_claims.factor: about 74x lower T-depth for Usqrt than Usin
speedup_claims.conditions: n = 15, d = 20, comparator-based Usqrt versus controlled-Ry-based Usin
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states Usin requires T-depth about 818 while Usqrt requires 11 for the n = 15 case, giving roughly 74x difference.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Not given as asymptotic complexity; resource estimate is 4.7k logical qubits, T-depth 4.5e7, T-count 2.4e9 for the benchmark instance.
complexity_analysis.constant_factor_quantum: Usqrt-QSP improves over arithmetic benchmark by about 4.7x in T-depth, 16x in T-count, and 4.1x in qubits; logical clock rate reduced from 207 MHz to 45 MHz.
complexity_analysis.wall_clock_quantum: 1 second classical-equivalent target runtime assumed; quantum processor needs 45 MHz T-gate rate to match it

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Reported benchmark resources for the QSP Usqrt approach are 4.7k logical qubits, T-depth 4.5e7, and T-count 2.4e9; the paper compares these to an arithmetic baseline but does not demonstrate a practical runtime advantage on hardware.
limiting_factors: Advantage is only a resource-estimate comparison, not an executed benchmark

notes: The paper explicitly reports the end-to-end resource estimate for the autocallable benchmark: 4.7k logical qubits, T-depth 4.5e7, T-count 2.4e9, and 45 MHz logical clock rate for quantum advantage.
The paper compares against an arithmetic-based prior method and states the improvement factors; no actual hardware execution is reported.
The paper reports a theoretical resource estimate for an autocallable benchmark and compares it against an arithmetic-based prior method; it does not claim a demonstrated practical quantum advantage.
